testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When should placards be used?

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is empty space in the truck.
If hazardous materials weigh more than 200 pounds.
If hazardous materials can be inhaled.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They show what type of materials are being carried and warn others about the hazards.

questions.question: Drivers often tailgate trucks in bad weather.
questions.explanation: Many drivers follow large trucks too closely in bad weather when visibility is poor. You should respond safely to tailgaters instead of speeding up.

questions.question: What part of the truck is the air compressor connected to?
questions.explanation: The air compressor connects to the engine using gears or a belt.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other drivers, you should:

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you. Check local laws to make sure this is allowed.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.explanation: Air brakes use compressed air to function.

questions.question: Which of these can help you know when to upshift?
questions.explanation: Two things help you know when to shift up. First, watch engine speed (rpm). Read your manual to learn when to shift based on rpm. Second, watch road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, then watch your speedometer and shift as needed.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Help drivers see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often have curved convex mirrors. These mirrors let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
A driver making a single pull-up.
A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and using the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle crossing over an exercise boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of the vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the test. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control test, what is an encroachment?

options.text: A driver putting the vehicle in neutral and using the parking brake.
The vehicle touching a boundary line.
A driver completing an exercise correctly.
An applicant trying to bribe the examiner.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle touching a boundary line.
questions.explanation: An encroachment happens when any part of the vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line during the test. Each encroachment counts as an error.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Keep driving but have the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop the vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes. Inspect and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: The tires lose contact with the road.
The vehicle is easier to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires slide on water instead of gripping the road. The tires lose contact with the road surface.

questions.question: Is there a penalty for refusing to take a blood alcohol test?
questions.explanation: Minnesota has an Implied Consent Law. When you drive in Minnesota, you agree to take a chemical test if police ask. If you refuse, your license will be revoked for one year and you cannot operate a CMV for one year.

questions.question: A CMV driver with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) lower than 0.04 percent will be:

options.text: Taken out of service for 24 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taken out of service for 24 hours.
questions.explanation: If you drive a CMV with any amount of alcohol in your system below 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for 24 hours. Driving with any alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Why must drivers inspect their vehicles?

options.text: Federal and state laws require it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Federal and state laws require it.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving to make sure they are safe.

questions.question: What do header boards do?

options.text: They protect the driver from being hit by cargo.
They protect the driver's head when entering the truck cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: They protect the driver from being hit by cargo.
questions.explanation: Header boards, also called headache racks, protect the driver if cargo moves forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brakes three times, then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brakes three times, then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should slowly move toward the floor.
Pump the brakes three times, then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.
Pump the brakes three times, then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should be easy to push to the floor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes three times, then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times, then press hard and hold for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it moves, there may be a leak.

questions.question: What about height warnings on low bridges?

options.text: Height warnings must always be posted.
Height warnings must be posted at least twice.
Height warnings may be posted, but are not required.

questions.correctAnswerText: Height warnings may be posted, but are not required.
questions.explanation: Height warnings are often posted on low bridges, but not always. If you are unsure if your vehicle will clear an overhead object, drive slowly and carefully.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving only during certain hours.
Honk at other drivers to make them move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, such as driving only during certain hours.
questions.explanation: Oversized loads need special permits. They can only be driven at certain times and may require special warning signs or equipment.

questions.question: When traveling long distances, you should:
questions.explanation: Take a break after every 100 miles or two hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving when you would normally be sleeping is dangerous.

questions.question: ____ are most affected by strong winds.
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to control your vehicle. Lighter CMVs are especially at risk.

questions.question: What happens if an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) malfunctions?

options.text: A yellow warning light will turn on in the instrument panel.

questions.correctAnswerText: A yellow warning light will turn on in the instrument panel.
questions.explanation: When ABS malfunctions, a yellow warning light appears on the instrument panel. This alerts you that the braking system needs attention.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what happens when air pressure is lost and spring brakes activate?

options.text: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
You can use spring brakes to continue driving normally.
The air tanks automatically refill to safe pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time.
questions.explanation: A separate air tank can temporarily release spring brakes if they activate from low air pressure. Pushing the correct control releases the brakes briefly, letting you move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: In an emergency while driving, should you always stop?
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the safest response in an emergency. Steering away from danger is usually safer than stopping.

questions.question: Is rough acceleration good for your vehicle?

options.text: Yes, it is fine at slow speeds.
Yes, it is fine at all speeds.
No, it can damage the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it can damage the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerate smoothly and gradually. Rough acceleration can cause mechanical damage to your vehicle.

questions.question: When starting a commercial vehicle, does the oil pressure gauge take about one minute to show normal pressure?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should rise to normal within seconds after starting the engine. If pressure is low, dropping, or changing, stop driving immediately.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: For speeds below 40 mph, maintain one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. For higher speeds, add one more second.

questions.question: How much water on a road surface can cause hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water. It does not require much water to occur.

questions.question: If a load is 10 feet long, what is the minimum number of tie-downs needed?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo must have at least two tie-downs, regardless of size.

questions.question: What tool should you use to check tire inflation?
questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check tire pressure during vehicle inspection. Kicking tires does not count as a proper check.

questions.question: If you are unsure how to put out a vehicle fire, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you do not know which type of fire extinguisher to use, especially for hazardous materials fires, wait for firefighters to arrive and handle it.

questions.question: You should always be able to stop within:

options.text: Your view of the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your view of the road ahead.
questions.explanation: You must be able to stop your vehicle within the distance you can see ahead. Slow down when visibility is reduced.

questions.question: A steering wheel should be held:

options.text: With one hand, keeping the other hand free for other tasks.
With one hand at a time, alternating between hands.
At the base of the wheel.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: Which crime would NOT disqualify someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Certain crimes disqualify you from a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include kidnapping, smuggling, and immigration violations. Speeding is not on this list.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brake pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly down.
Pump the brake pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times, then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times and then push hard for five seconds. The pedal should stay in place. If it moves, you may have a leak or another problem.

questions.question: On a flatbed trailer, a load does not need to be tied down if it is heavy enough.
questions.explanation: All cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to prevent it from moving or falling off. Follow the tie-down rules for your specific cargo.

questions.question: To avoid slowing down traffic when driving a large truck, you should:

options.text: Try to pass another vehicle while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane whenever possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane whenever possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy truck cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Check important items only at the start and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Check important items only at the start and end of a trip
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during a trip, not just at the start and end. Watch the gauges, check mirrors, look at tires and cargo, and use all your senses to catch problems early.

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle is unsafe, they can:

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix the vehicle.
Formally ask you to fix the vehicle's problems.
Take the vehicle out of service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take the vehicle out of service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: Federal or state inspectors can take an unsafe vehicle out of service until the problems are fixed.

questions.question: If you stop on the side of a highway, how far behind your vehicle should warning devices go?
questions.explanation: Place warning devices 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet behind your vehicle when stopped on a highway.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
Make sure the vehicle is inspected on a regular schedule
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: When checking tires, which of the following is NOT a problem?

options.text: At least 4/32 inch of tread in the grooves on front tires
Using radial and bias-ply tires together

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 4/32 inch of tread in the grooves on front tires
questions.explanation: When checking tires, air pressure should not be too low or too high. Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires together.

questions.question: During the CDL vehicle inspection test, you may be asked to:
questions.explanation: The CDL vehicle inspection test includes checking the engine oil level.

questions.question: How long must carriers keep fuel records for IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns?
questions.explanation: Carriers must keep mileage and fuel records that support IFTA quarterly fuel tax returns for four years.

questions.question: Excessive vibration may be a sign of tire failure.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle thumps or vibrates heavily, a tire may have failed. Check your tires as soon as you can safely pull over.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal should be:

options.text: Pressed down quickly with both feet

questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down gradually to ensure a smooth, safe stop.

questions.question: When doing pre-trip inspections, what should you do?

options.text: Do the inspection the same way each time
Check items in a different order each time
Skip some items if you are in a hurry

questions.correctAnswerText: Do the inspection the same way each time
questions.explanation: Do pre-trip inspections the same way every time. This habit makes it less likely you will forget to check something important.

questions.question: Front brake limiting valves were designed to:

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding
Stop the front tires from overheating

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding
questions.explanation: Some older air brake vehicles have front brake limiting valves. These were designed to reduce front wheel skidding. Research shows they are not needed, so they should be left in the "normal" position.

questions.question: Is texting while driving allowed?

options.text: Yes, if you are contacting your employer
Yes, when driving on rural roads

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and never permitted while operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: How often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: Only if you think there is a problem

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic and watch for problems on your vehicle.
